title: Fatherhood of God
definition: The fatherhood of God refers to His identity as Father within the Trinity and His gracious relationship to believers adopted through Christ.
summary: God is Father, and believers know Him as Father through Jesus Christ.
christFocus: Jesus reveals the Father and brings believers into the family of God through adoption.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
God is eternally Father in relation to the Son, and He becomes Father to believers by grace through adoption. Not every use of fatherhood in Scripture means the same thing, but all reveal His authority, care, provision, and love.

Believers do not earn the right to call God Father. Through Christ, they receive the Spirit of adoption and are welcomed into God's family.

The fatherhood of God is perfect, unlike broken earthly examples. He disciplines, provides, loves, hears, and keeps His children.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Earthly father wounds can distort how people think of God. The fatherhood of God matters because Scripture reveals a Father who is holy, faithful, compassionate, and good.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Approach God as Father through Christ. Bring your needs, fears, failures, and worship to Him, and let His perfect fatherhood reshape broken assumptions.
